title: Resolution on the return of the Romanian national treasure
author: European Parliament
locator: P9_TA(2024)0171; recitals D, I and paragraph 7
finding: States the claim as 91.5 tonnes of fine gold; records partial cultural returns and the joint commission’s acknowledgement of authentic deposit documents.
caution: A political resolution, not a court judgment, contemporary vault inspection, or recovery order.

title: The NBR treasure sent to Moscow — document portal
author: National Bank of Romania
access: Portal and rendered sections read; selected scans inspected
finding: The bank announced inventories, historical images and copies of original documents from its own archive.
caution: Initial text retrieval returned navigation; a subsequent browser pass reached the collection. Four selected protocol/annex photographs were visually inspected, not the complete archive. See S41–S43.

title: Cum arată Tezaurul României de la Moscova
author: Cristina Stancu, Adevărul, reproducing BNR material
locator: Chronology; Prima restituire (1935); A doua restituire (1956)
finding: Detailed shipment values and return procedures: 1935 via Odesa and Constanța; 1956 art, coins and medals, not the BNR reserve.
caution: Same evidence family as BNR, not independent corroboration. Its two shipment values do not sum to its stated total; its 1956 category counts also differ from its headline total.

title: Tezaurul României la Moscova. 100 de ani mai târziu
author: National History Museum of Romania (MNIR)
locator: Centenary exhibition announcement and appended governor’s remarks
finding: Identifies Pietroasele as a returned, viewable treasure; says the National Art Museum’s 1956 return-inventory registers were exhibited. Lists what BNR actually received in 1935.
caution: An exhibition announcement and quoted institutional address, not the underlying accession registers. Rounded gold totals here differ slightly from the current 91.5-tonne claim.

title: Destinul Tezaurului României. Argumente din arhivele ruse
author: Ilie Schipor; Oscar Print
finding: Author’s reconstruction: partial evacuation in October 1919, return in July 1921, progressive expenditure from autumn 1921 through early 1925.
caution: The full 448-page book was not obtained. The publisher’s summary is not a substitute for its document annexes.

title: Destinul Tezaurului României — publisher sample
author: Ilie Schipor
finding: Includes the opening archival document and facsimiles: Bark to Alekseev, 28 October 1916, concerning the evacuation proposal.
caution: Only a sample. It does not contain the decisive 1924 report, document 121. Citation given for document 1: RGVIA, f. 2003, op. 1, d. 1474, l. 221 recto/verso; original archive not visited.

title: Tezaurul BNR între Cazaciocul dezinformării și „Răsucita” româno-rusă (I)
author: Ilie Schipor interview / AFnews
access: Written article read; embedded video not watched
locator: Discussion comparing the 16 February 1917 inventory with the 23 May 1921 RGAE report
finding: Schipor explicitly argues that the gold remained intact through May 1921, based on a denomination-by-denomination comparison.
caution: The original May 1921 inventory and full comparison have not been independently audited. This is the researcher’s claim, not our own verified gram-level reconciliation.

title: „Soarta” sau „destinul” Tezaurului României
author: Ilie Schipor, Arhivele Totalitarismului
finding: Abstract rejects several civil-war disappearance explanations and places final expenditure in the mid-1920s.
caution: Full text requires access; not purchased or read. Same author and research family as S05–S07.

title: Romania’s Treasury — guarded by the Russian “ally”
author: Viorica Moisuc, Minerva
access: Full PDF obtained; relevant passages read
locator: Vol. 2, issue 1, pp. 27–76; especially pp. 72–74 and notes 96–103
finding: Reproduces a translated 13 December 1924 report describing 1919 relocations and subsequent overseas disposal of specified coin groups.
caution: The URL’s 2024 upload date is not the publication date. Strongly polemical framing; translations are mediated through Schipor. The reproduced report contains an ambiguous numerical expression.

title: Судьба «румынского золота» в России 1916–2020. Очерки истории
author: Tatyana A. Pokivaylova, Aletheia / Institute of Slavic Studies RAS
access: Full 268-page PDF obtained; relevant chapters read
finding: Russian archival synthesis acknowledges gold still recorded in 1922 and described as обезличено by 1924; discusses inventories, returns and competing debt claims.
caution: Some eastward routes are explicitly speculative. Two conflicting 1922 balances are quoted. “Depersonalized” does not by itself prove melting. Archive-access statements describe conditions when the book was written.

title: Amintiri — including Jurnalul de la Moscova
author: Alexandru Lapedatu; edited by Ioan Opriș
access: Full volume obtained; Moscow diary passages read
locator: Printed pp. 117–121, 129–130, 142, 151, 155–158; PDF page = printed page + 4
finding: Day-by-day account of packing, departure, observed railway stops, damp storage, later relocation, and proposed evacuation to America.
caution: Published transcription, not the handwritten notebook inspected. Lapedatu supervised cultural consignments, not an audit of all bullion. Download is for personal reading; this site does not redistribute the book.

title: Francis reports the Soviet retention of Romanian gold
author: US Ambassador David R. Francis to Secretary of State
locator: FRUS 1918, Russia vol. II, doc. 836; file 871.51/110
finding: Contemporary US diplomatic evidence that the Soviet authorities held the gold and that Romania sought Allied intervention.
caution: A diplomatic report, not a physical count. Its valuation must not be treated as a weighed gold quantity.

title: Further request for Allied protest over Romanian gold
author: US Ambassador David R. Francis
finding: Documents the immediate dispute and pressure for a formal Allied protest.
caution: Shows diplomacy and contemporary knowledge; cannot establish the reserve’s later route.

title: Treasury explains treatment of Soviet gold and Swedish mint stamps
author: Assistant Secretary of the Treasury S. P. Gilbert Jr. to Assistant Secretary of State Fred M. Dearing
finding: Explains the distinction between gold suspected of Soviet origin and gold bearing the official stamp of a friendly country’s mint, including Sweden.
caution: Documents a generic route and administrative rules. It does not identify a Romanian consignment.

title: State Department’s position on foreign-mint gold
author: Fred M. Dearing to S. P. Gilbert Jr.
finding: Discusses title, friendly-country mint marks, and why Treasury must decide what the US mints accept.
caution: Not a certificate that particular gold had clean title, nor proof of Romanian gold in Swedish bars.

title: The S.S. Carmania gold shipment rejected at New York
author: S. P. Gilbert Jr. to the Secretary of State
finding: Records 7,500 imperial gold roubles consigned by the Bank of England to J. P. Morgan & Co.; the New York Assay Office rejected the tender on 10 August.
caution: No Romanian provenance is stated. This is a negative control against turning every Soviet gold shipment into “the Romanian treasure.”

title: Romanian memorandum alleging gold reaching the United States
author: Romanian Legation to the US Department of State
finding: Romania alleged that part of the gold reaching the US was its 1916 deposit being used for Soviet payments abroad.
caution: The memorandum names no ship, bank, weight, assay lot or informant. Authentic evidence of an allegation, not authentication of a shipment.

title: Boyle, Joseph Whiteside
author: William Rodney, Dictionary of Canadian Biography
locator: Moscow mission, December 1917; bibliography at end
finding: Explicitly distinguishes Boyle’s recovery of archives and paper currency from later claims about bullion and crown jewels.
caution: Retrospective scholarship. The precise contents should ultimately be checked against mission and receiving inventories.

title: British Adventurers and Revolutionary Russia’s War over Bessarabia
author: Geoffrey Swain, Revolutionary Russia
access: Full open-access PDF obtained; relevant passages read
finding: Locates Boyle material in PRONI D1943 and British diplomatic papers; retells a jewels claim through George Hill’s memoir.
caution: Its introductory shipment summary repeats problematic quantities. A memoir-derived jewel story is not a BNR gold recovery manifest.

title: Queen Marie of Romania papers — finding aid
author: Kent State University Special Collections
locator: Box 1; subseries 1D on Boyle and the Romanian treasure
finding: Identifies correspondence and later investigations, including 1946 and 1990 material, useful for tracing how the rescue legend developed.
caution: A catalogue is not the correspondence itself. Much is decades later than the events; no inspected 1917 treasure notebook here.

title: Bucarest, légation puis ambassade, 1916–1980 — finding aid
author: Archives diplomatiques, France
access: Full finding aid obtained; relevant entries read
finding: Locates Russian/Romanian correspondence and French military-mission records for the critical custody and diplomatic period.
caution: Underlying files not inspected. Series relevance does not prove a treasure document is inside. Early wartime destruction also creates gaps.

title: Din presa vremii: Glasul Bucovinei despre Tezaurul românesc, 1920
author: Ion N. Oprea, Luceafărul
access: Modern transcription read; original issues not inspected
locator: Glasul Bucovinei no. 465, 10 July 1920; also nos. 453, 474, 558; cites Oprea’s 2008 book, pp. 115–116
finding: Transcribes a report alleging Romanian 20-lei coins pledged in Danish banks, attributed to an unnamed Copenhagen newspaper.
caution: A multi-step quotation chain. The Danish newspaper, banks, coin lots and original Romanian scan remain unidentified or unread.

title: Glasul Bucovinei digitized collection
author: LIBRARIA, Ukrainian periodicals archive
access: Collection record read; target issue not inspected
locator: Target: no. 465, 10 July 1920; alternative collection at adt.arcanum.com
finding: A concrete route to obtaining the original newspaper behind the Danish-bank allegation.
caution: Listing coverage does not establish that this exact issue is accessible without an account or subscription.

title: Tezaurul României la Moscova după 1989: Odiseea continuă
author: Historia
locator: Private schemes and the 12-coin donation narrative
finding: Reports twelve French and Belgian coins, total 77.09 g, connected to a private arrangement and a 2008 museum donation.
caution: Museum accession documentation and original custody proof were not obtained. Genuine nineteenth-century coins do not establish origin in the Moscow deposit.

title: The Romanian National Bank Treasure Taken to Moscow and Never Returned
author: Cristian Păunescu; foreword Mugur Isărescu; Oscar Print
locator: ISBN 978-973-668-529-3; calendar note p. 3; opening account pp. 13–16
finding: Useful calendar warning and account of the diplomatic pressure preceding evacuation.
caution: Not the complete book. Older quantity and value conventions should not override the current fine-gold claim without reconciliation.

title: Tezaurul român de la Moscova (1934) — located edition
author: Mihail Gr. Romașcanu; modern Ziaristi Online presentation
access: Book located; full text not obtained
finding: Important early compilation to compare with later inventories and retellings.
caution: The surrounding website is not the book. No claim here is based on pretending the embedded book was read.

title: The Gold Treasure of National Bank of Romania from Moscow between history and politics
author: Nadia Manea
finding: Recent synthesis distinguishes the 91.5-tonne reserve from identity/cultural treasure and discusses the 2024 resolution.
caution: Full article not obtained; abstract only. Substantially draws on the same official and Schipor evidence families.

title: A new strategy for recovery of the Romanian treasure
author: Radio România Actualități
locator: Reporting on a proposed memorandum and strategy
finding: Shows the recovery issue remained active in 2026.
caution: A proposed strategy is not a signed return agreement, shipment or recovered gold.

title: Russian response to the European Parliament’s gold demand
author: RBC, reporting Maria Zakharova’s statements
locator: Response on debt offsets, returns and Soviet-era claims
finding: Documents Russia’s public counter-position and its use of broader historical financial claims.
caution: Political assertions are not itemized custody records. No audited ledger is supplied to establish that the BNR reserve was repaid.

title: Claim that Russia offered the treasure back and Romania refused
author: Veridica
finding: Examines a circulating story of a refused private return arrangement.
caution: A fact-check is not an archive inspection. No authenticated current holding or inventory was found through this story.

title: Rușii au găsit, în propriile arhive, documente despre Tezaurul României (I)
author: Ilie Schipor; Cetatea Cavalerilor article reprinted by ActiveNews
access: Written article and inventory-table image inspected
locator: Table headed “Numărul de: lăzi / saci”; discussion of Mosyakin’s 2021 volumes
finding: Reconstructs the first shipment by denomination: German marks 45.56%, Austrian crowns 29.31%, Romanian caroli 0.34% of stated BNR value.
caution: An author’s modern table, not the original ledger. Values and case rows reconcile; its Austrian row says 4,397 bags, versus 4,387 in the BNR annex photograph and transcription (S41–S42). The latter reconciles the printed 13,823 total. Host commentary is not endorsed.

title: Золото Российской империи и большевики. 1917–1922 гг.
author: Aleksandr G. Mosyakin; Mezhdunarodnye otnosheniya
access: Publisher record and search excerpts; full volumes not read
locator: Three volumes; ISBN 978-5-7133-1649-5; publisher advertises 742 documents
finding: Potential independent access path to RGAE facsimiles cited in Schipor’s later comparison.
caution: Publisher’s broad political framing is not a finding. Preview download timed out; exact Romanian entries and shelfmarks require the volumes.

title: British test case concerning Soviet gold
author: US Ambassador George Harvey
finding: Context for the 7,500-rouble shipment later recorded on the Carmania.
caution: A Russian bondholder and Russian gold case, not an established Romanian claim.

title: Tezaurul României de la Moscova prin noi documente ruse și sovietice
author: George Popescu / Radio România Actualități, with Ilie Schipor
access: Written article read; broadcast not transcribed
finding: Contemporary account of the new Russian-archive research and why it changed the disappearance narrative.
caution: The same Schipor work, not a separate archive audit.

title: Romanian Treasure
author: Wikipedia contributors
finding: A useful starting index of names, returns and popular explanations.
caution: The approximately 120-tonne wording is not the current fine-gold claim. This investigation does not rely on Wikipedia as decisive evidence.

title: Alexandru Lapedatu — publications and archive references
author: Lapedatu family foundation
finding: Provides a discovery route to the published diary and further Lapedatu material.
caution: A guide, not an additional independent eyewitness.

title: The Odyssey of the Romanian treasure taken to Moscow
author: Ion Jinga / Romanian Permanent Representation to the Council of Europe
finding: Useful record of official advocacy and a competing published quantity convention.
caution: Not fully fetched. Do not silently reconcile its older quantity or wagon count with newer official figures.

title: The expulsion of the Romanian Legation
author: US Ambassador David R. Francis
finding: Independent contemporary record of the diplomatic rupture surrounding seizure.
caution: Does not inventory the treasure.

title: Romania: from 1880 to 1947
author: George Virgil Stoenescu, Adriana Aloman, Elisabeta Blejan and Brîndușa Grațiela Costache; hosted by BNR
access: Full PDF obtained; monetary-standard section read
locator: Chapter VI; section 1.2, printed pp. 244–247; monetary-standard table
finding: Documents 0.3226 g of mint gold at 900‰ per leu, and 3,100 lei per kg of 900‰ gold. Also describes removal of the Moscow deposit from note-cover stock in 1929.
caution: A monetary-history synthesis, not an assay of the treasure. Removing an asset from currency-cover calculations does not prove physical repayment or legal discharge.

title: Сводка о наличии ценностей на 1 февраля 1922 г.
author: Commission for accounting and concentration of valuables; published in a 2018 document edition
access: Catalogue and published-document web transcription read
locator: Document 236, printed p. 391; RGASPI f. 19, op. 1, d. 492, l. 108; certified-copy description
finding: A concrete Soviet accounting comparison distinguishes usable coin, defective coin, bullion/scrap and valuable objects, producing different totals as categories are added. It is a useful control on what a gold balance means.
caution: The inspected account does not identify a Romanian component. Its 217.2 / 218.4 / 244.9-million-rouble totals must not be substituted for a Romanian inventory or used to resolve Pokivaylova’s two Romanian-specific balances. Archive original not inspected.

title: First-shipment inventory annex and selected protocol facsimiles
author: National Bank of Romania, publishing Russian/French deposit records
locator: Annex image 984499206.jpg; protocol first page 1266638180.jpg, last page 210295509.jpg; operations annex 220870989.jpg, linked from S42
finding: The summary annex visibly gives 4,387 Austrian-crown bags and a total of 13,823 bags. Selected protocol pages identify parties, seals, guards and a four-copy document arrangement.
caution: Selected institutional photographs, not a complete protocol or an archive visit. The Romanian-coin lei-value cell appears to read 1,065,000, while its currency amount and the official transcription give 1,065,705; the latter reconciles the grand total. Do not describe every original cell as independently reconciled. No 1921 or 1924 original is supplied here.

title: Inventarul tezaurului / Treasure inventory
author: National Bank of Romania
access: Both rendered language versions read; linked scans inspected
locator: English counterpart: https://www.bnr.ro/en/24934-treasure-inventory; denomination table and final paragraph
finding: Official table uses 4,387 Austrian-crown bags. Romanian text places the additional four gold cases in summer 1917. The reserve is described as 91.5 tonnes of fine gold.
caution: English final paragraph says December 1917 for the additional four cases, unlike Romanian summer 1917 and the history chronology. This is a language-version inconsistency, not evidence for a third shipment. The table is a transcription and has to be distinguished from the facsimile.

title: Treasure history
author: National Bank of Romania
finding: Direct institutional source for the two shipment values, August 1917 additional deposit, and return accounts.
caution: Its stated total 315,179,980.41 gold lei is 25,000 above its stated components. This discrepancy is therefore present on BNR itself, not merely in a newspaper reprint. Institutional summaries are not infallible; originals should control.
